description_full: Lennar Corporation, together with its subsidiaries, operates as a homebuilder primarily under the Lennar brand in the United States. It operates through Homebuilding East, Homebuilding Central, Homebuilding South Central, Homebuilding West, Financial Services, Multifamily, and Lennar Other segments. The company's homebuilding operations include the construction and sale of single-family attached and detached homes, as well as the purchase, development, and sale of residential land; and development, construction, and management of multifamily rental properties. It also offers residential mortgage financing, title insurance, and closing services for home buyers and others, as well as originating and selling securitization commercial mortgage loans. In addition, the company is involved in fund investment activities. It primarily serves first-time, move-up, active adult, and luxury homebuyers. The company was founded in 1954 and is based in Miami, Florida.

financial_summary: Lennar Corporation is a large-cap consumer cyclical business with a $19.9B market cap on $34.2B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +8% over the past three years and +14% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 16% against a 8% cost of capital, a 8-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.

The business throws off $28M in free cash flow — roughly 0 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders. Cash conversion is thin at 0.10×, however, which raises the oldest question in analysis: are these earnings backed by cash?.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.7× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 57× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 11.7% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 16% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
